Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:6: In the Zohar (portion Bereshit, end of 56) they were also strict about the punishment for this sin. These are his words: Rabbi Yehuda opened (Psalms 5:5), "for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You" — this verse has been discussed and established, but come and see: whoever attaches himself to the evil inclination and is drawn after it becomes impure, as it is said (Genesis 6:5), "for the wickedness of man was great" — they did all manner of evil, and their sin was not complete until they poured out seed in vain upon the earth; and who are these? Those who corrupted their way upon the earth. This is what is written, "only evil all the day" — here it is written "only evil," and there it is written "evil shall not sojourn with You," and it is written (Genesis 38:10), "and Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of the LORD."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:7: Rabbi Yosi said, is not "evil" the same as "wicked"? He said to him, no — even one who merely raises his hand against his fellow, even though he does nothing to him, is called "wicked," as it is written (Exodus 2:13), "and he said to the wicked one, why do you strike your fellow?" — it is not written "you struck" but "you strike" [implying merely raising a hand]. But one is called "evil" [rah] only if he corrupts his way and defiles himself, and defiles the earth, and gives strength and power to the impure spirit called "evil," as it is written, "only evil all the day" — and he does not enter the palace and does not see the face of the Shechinah, since through this the Shechinah departs from the world. From where do we learn this? From Jacob — for when the Shechinah departed from him, it was because he thought there was unfitness among his sons, for through them the impure spirit was strengthened and it diminished and blemished the light of the moon. And should you ask why — because this one [Reuven] defiled the sanctuary and the Shechinah departed from upon Jacob; all the more so, one who corrupts his way and defiles himself, who strengthens the impure spirit — therefore, when he becomes defiled he is called "evil." Come and see: when a person becomes defiled he is never again visited for good, and he is always visited by that which is called "evil" for ill — this is what is written (Proverbs 19:23), "and satisfied, he shall lodge without being visited by evil" — when he walks in the straight path, then he is not visited by evil; therefore it is written "only evil all the day," and it is written "evil shall not sojourn with You" — behold, he is called "evil" and not "wicked," and it is written (Psalms 23:4), "even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:8: Behold, his punishment is explained: he does not see the face of the Shechinah and does not enter the palace, and this is because of the reasons mentioned in the statement. The first, that it says "he defiles himself" — through arousing the spirit of impurity in all his limbs by the power of that heating up in which he heated himself, since the drop of seed cannot come out except through the heating of all the limbs, so his limbs are found to become impure. This is somewhat similar to the sin of anger, which is explained in portion Tetzaveh (182b) — that one who becomes heated with anger defiles himself within and without.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:9: Therefore it is explained in the Zohar (portion Vayeshev, 188a) that there is no sin that defiles a person more than the sin of seed in vain. These are his words: come and see, among all the sins by which a person becomes defiled in this world, this is the sin by which a person becomes more defiled, in this world and in the World to Come — one who casts his seed emptily, and emits his seed emptily by hand or foot and becomes defiled by it, as it is said (Psalms 5:5), "for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You." Because of this he does not enter behind the curtain and does not see the countenance of the Ancient of Days, as we have learned — here it is written, "evil shall not sojourn with You," and there it is written, "and Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of the LORD," and therefore (Isaiah 1:15), "your hands are full of blood." Fortunate is the portion of a person who fears his Master and is guarded from the evil way, and purifies himself to occupy himself in the fear of his Master. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:10: He further says, "and defiles the earth" — meaning, he defiles the supernal earth [Malchut]. The reason is that the supernal earth receives its flow only from the supernal Tzadik, and the Tzadik bestows only upon her; and when a person heats himself in vain, he causes the supernal covenant to become enslaved to bestow the good supernal flow upon the external forces — for the secret of its establishment, in the secret of (Genesis 17:21), "and My covenant I will establish with Isaac," comes through the arousal of Torah and good deeds, to bestow the light of supernal whiteness upon her; and when he has a nocturnal emission, being heated through Lilith and her powers, this too is in vain — and all vanity and emptiness belong to the external forces, like the nation who bows to "vanity and emptiness." We find that the flow which the Mistress [the Shechinah] should have received is received by the maidservant, so that "the maidservant inherits from her mistress," and the Mistress receives the leftover, which is the harsh judgment from the side of the left — this is "and defiles the earth." And whoever knows the secret of the supernal union knows how grave this sin is.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:11: "And gives strength and power to the impure spirit" — this is explained by what we have written. Therefore, measure for measure: just as the blemish was in the Shechinah, so he does not receive the face of the Shechinah; and just as he gave the spirit of impurity dominion over himself, so his soul will not enter the palace, which is the secret of holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:12: And he says at the end of the statement, "come and see, when a person becomes defiled he is not [favorably] visited" — explained along the lines of what is explained in the Gemara, tractate Berachot (14a): Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, whoever satisfies himself with words of Torah and goes to sleep is not brought bad news, as it is said (Proverbs 19:23), "and satisfied, he shall lodge without being visited by evil." Thus far his words. And according to the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, this "evil" mentioned in the verse is one who emits seed in vain, meaning that he will not come to a nocturnal emission when he is satisfied with words of Torah, since words of Torah are a remedy for this illness, as we shall further explain. And his meaning in saying "when a person becomes defiled" etc. is that as long as he has not repented from this sin, he is not visited in his dream by the Holy One, blessed be He, for good; on the contrary, since the external forces have gained dominion over him, he becomes their portion, and they visit him with evil and defile him with a nocturnal emission — this is what is meant by "and he is always visited by that which is called 'evil' for ill."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:13: Especially if he wishes to enter into the inner wisdom, into the place of secret, and he is blemished in the attribute of Tzadik, which is the secret — he is pushed away from there, and they defile him to show him that he is not fit to enter there; and this is proven in the Zohar (portion Naso, 123a). And so they said in Tikkunim, the first Tikkun (17b), these are his words: "Bereshit" — two "reshit" [beginnings] — "this is the gate of the LORD, the righteous shall enter through it" (Psalms 118:20) — this is the gate of the righteous, who have permission to enter there, while others who are not righteous are pushed away from there. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:14: Further, in the Zohar (portion Noach, 62a): come and see, all of a person's sins, all his corruptions, depend on repentance; but the sin of one who casts his seed and corrupts his way and emits seed upon the earth corrupts himself and corrupts the earth — of him it is written (Jeremiah 2:22), "your iniquity is stained before Me," and it is written of him (Psalms 5:5), "for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You," and it is written (Genesis 38:7), "and Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD put him to death," and this has already been said. Thus far his words. And in some handwritten manuscripts it is written: "except through the power of powerful repentance."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:15: Further, in the Zohar (portion Noach, beginning of 69), these are his words: among all the sins of the guilty of the world that push away the Shechinah, one of them is one who corrupts his way upon the earth, as we have said; and therefore he does not see the face of the Shechinah and does not enter the palace, and of these it is written (Genesis 7:23), "and they were blotted out from the earth" — they were blotted out entirely. Come and see: at the time the Holy One, blessed be He, will revive the dead, all those dead found outside, in other foreign lands, the Holy One, blessed be He, will create their bodies as fitting, etc., but the Holy One, blessed be He, gives souls only in the land of Israel, as it is written (Ezekiel 37:12), "behold, I open your graves and bring you up from your graves, My people, and I will bring you to the land of Israel" — that they roll beneath the earth [to the land of Israel]; and afterward what is written? (ibid. 37:14), "and I will put My spirit within you and you shall live" etc. — for in the land of Israel all the people of the world will receive their souls, except these who defiled themselves and defiled the earth — of these it is written, precisely, "and they were blotted out from the earth," and although the early ones disputed this, [saying that] "blotted out" is as in (Psalms 69:29), "let them be blotted out of the book of life." Rabbi Shimon said to him: certainly they have no portion in the World to Come, as it is written, "and they were blotted out from the earth," and it is written (Isaiah 60:21), "forever they shall inherit the land" [implying these will not] — but they will arise in judgment, and of them it is said (Daniel 12:2), "and many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, these" [to judgment]. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:16: Although this statement speaks of the generation of the Flood, who have no portion in the World to Come, and according to Rabbi Abba's view they will not rise in resurrection nor in judgment at all — nevertheless we learn from it that whoever, in this generation, does as they did and does not repent will have no portion in the World to Come; and even if he rises in judgment, according to Rashbi's view, it will be to disgrace — for since the essential reason given for the generation of the Flood having no portion in the World to Come is that they poured out their seed upon the earth, as it is written (Genesis 6:12), "for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth," and this is what caused them to be blotted out from the earth entirely, both above and below — so it will be for anyone who does as they did and does not repent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:17: And in the Zohar (portion Vayechi, 219b) they were likewise strict about the severity of this sin, on the verse (Isaiah 3:11), "woe to the wicked evil one, for the deed of his hands shall be done to him." These are his words: why "for the deed of his hands"? Rabbi Yitzchak said, this includes one who fornicates with his hand, to emit and corrupt his seed in vain — he is called "evil" and does not see the face of the Shechinah (Psalms 5:5), "for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You," and it is written (Genesis 38:10), "and Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil"; here too, "woe to the wicked evil one" — woe to that guilty one who is "evil," who makes himself evil; "for the deed of his hands shall be done to him" includes one who fornicates with his hand, to emit and corrupt his seed in vain, and this one is punished in that world more than all others. Come and see, for it is written "woe to the wicked evil one" — why "evil"? Rather, as we have said, he makes himself "evil"; and it is written, "evil shall not sojourn with You" — and all [other sinners] ascend [eventually to their place], but this one does not ascend. And should you say, what of other guilty ones who kill people — come and see, all of them ascend and he does not ascend. Why? Because they killed another person, but this one kills his own actual children, and sheds much blood. Come and see: regarding other guilty ones of the world it is not written "and it was evil in the eyes of the LORD," but here it is written (Genesis 38:10), "and what he did was evil in the eyes of the LORD" — why? Because it is written (ibid. 38:9), "and he spoiled it upon the ground."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:18: We have learned: Rabbi Yehuda said, there is no sin in the world for which there is no repentance except this one, and there are no wicked people who do not see the face of the Shechinah except these, as it is written, "evil shall not sojourn with You." Rabbi Yitzchak said, fortunate are the righteous in this world and in the World to Come; of them it is written (Isaiah 60:21), "and your people, all of them righteous, shall inherit the land forever" etc. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:19: Although this statement says, without qualification, that there is no repentance for this, we must resolve this matter, for we have learned that there is nothing for which there is no repentance — for the Holy One, blessed be He, accepted even Menasheh (Sanhedrin 103a). If so, how does this sin differ from all others?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:20: It seems to me to resolve this by saying that the intent is that this matter does not depend on lower repentance [teshuvah tata'ah], as with other blemishes whose beginning of return is through lower repentance — namely, immediately upon turning from evil they are accepted — and this is precise in the wording that follows: "and there are no wicked people who do not see the face of the Shechinah except these." The reason is that this sin is in the Tzadik and in the Shechinah together, as explained; therefore, since the Shechinah is its accuser, it does not accept it through [mere lower] repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:21: Through this we may understand the verse (Psalms 34:17), "the face of the LORD is against doers of evil, to cut off their remembrance from the earth; they cried out, and the LORD heard" — for "doers of evil" are those called emitters of seed in vain, and they are cut off from the land of the living because of the blemish therein; but "they cried out" and returned in repentance, "and the LORD heard" and saved them from all their troubles — as explained in the Zohar (portion Shemot, 20a): Rabbi Yehuda said, great is the outcry, for it tears up a person's decree throughout all his days; Rabbi Yitzchak says, great is the outcry, for it rules over the attribute of judgment above; Rabbi Yosi says, great is the outcry, for it rules in this world and in the World to Come — through outcry one inherits this world and the World to Come, as it is written (Psalms 107:6), "and they cried out to the LORD in their distress; He saved them from their afflictions." Thus far his words. We find, then, that the outcry is above ordinary lower repentance according to all interpretations, and therefore "the LORD heard." The intent is that his repentance is difficult until it reaches supernal repentance [teshuvah ila'ah].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:22: And likewise the sage, the honored Rabbi Yehuda Chalguah, peace be upon him, wrote in the book Tzafnat Pane'ach, that the intent in saying "there is no repentance for it" is that his repentance is extremely difficult, and he is not capable of doing the repentance [needed], since it requires many mortifications, and the penitent tires and does not do what is proper to do — this is [the meaning of] "there is no repentance for it." And also along the lines of what our Sages of blessed memory said (Avodah Zarah 17a), "all who come to her do not return" etc. (Proverbs 2:19), regarding one who has heresy, for whom it is hard to abandon his way, so he does not return.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:23: There is support for this view from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Zohar, portion Vayakhel, 214b), where he is strict about the severity of blemishing the sign of the covenant, saying at the end of his words: woe to that shameful one, from whom eternal vengeances are exacted — vengeance of this world and vengeance for that blemish. And he says afterward: these words apply when he has not done complete repentance, repentance sufficient to cover all his deeds. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:24: The reason he needs complete repentance to cover all his deeds is that the attribute of Tzadik is called "all" [kol], since all the attributes are included in it, as explained in Tikkunim (145b); and likewise the blemish in the covenant is a blemish in all the letters of YHVH, as explained in Tikkunim (131a): "Mi Yaaleh Lanu HaShamaymah" ["who shall go up for us to heaven"] — the initial letters spell MiLaH [circumcision], the final letters spell YHVH. We find, then, that whoever blemishes the covenant blemishes all the attributes included in the attribute of Tzadik and in the letters of the Name, and it is as though he has blemished the entire Shiur Komah [the whole cosmic "stature"]; therefore he requires complete repentance sufficient to cover all his deeds — for even though he has blemished all his limbs, he must act to correct all his limbs, as we shall explain. This can now be resolved another way: every [ordinary] repentance requires repentance [focused] on the organ with which one sinned, but the sin of the covenant does not depend on repentance of the covenant alone, as with, say, marrying a woman [to rectify adultery, etc.] — rather, powerful repentance is needed, as though he had blemished all his organs, as explained; and we shall elaborate further below.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:25: Proof that even those who emit seed in vain have a path to repentance: the generation of the Flood used to emit their seed in vain, and our Sages of blessed memory explained that Noah delayed in building the ark in order to proclaim to them that they should return and repent. They said in Midrash Tanchuma, portion Noach (§5): Rabbi Huna said in the name of Rabbi Yosi, for one hundred twenty years the Holy One, blessed be He, warned the generation of the Flood, in case they might repent; when they did not, He said to Noah (Genesis 6:14), "make yourself an ark of gopher wood" — Noah arose and planted cedars; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:26: My teacher, peace be upon him, wrote in the book Elimah regarding repentance for this sin, and I have summarized his words as follows: we find that he is called "evil" [rah], and evil is the opposite of good — for the Tzadik is called "good," since he causes the light of Yesod to be drawn to the female, since there flow the streams of the light of the supernal seed. Once he bestows this in vain, Lilith is found present there, she who is called "emptiness and vanity," and she causes the supernal covenant to become enslaved to bestow upon the external forces, and causes "the maidservant to inherit her mistress" — the flow that should have been bestowed on the Shechinah is bestowed on the external forces. Therefore he is called "evil," and therefore he does not see the face of the Shechinah — that is, the hidden good bestowed upon her — since he has blemished her, he will not merit that goodness after entering Gehinnom, which is not so for other sinners: for other sinners, after the measure of their sin's punishment in Gehinnom is completed, they enter the Garden of Eden to receive their reward, which is not so for one who blemished by emitting seed in vain. And there is no sin that defiles a person's soul more than emitting seed in vain — this if he has not repented; but if he has repented, there is nothing that stands before repentance. What they explained in the Zohar, that it does not depend on [ordinary] repentance, is that he must do things that are above the place of repentance — the reason being that one who blemishes the covenant blemishes the brain, since from there the seed flows, and he blemishes Chochmah; therefore he must do repentance above the place of [ordinary] repentance, which is Binah. This correction requires three things: first, repentance; second, wisdom [Chochmah]; third, humility. The repentance is to distance oneself from evil and attach oneself to good — namely, to perform adornments and unifications for the Shechinah, in such a way that, insofar as she was separated from the Tzadik, she should now look upon his face and Yesod bestow upon her. Likewise, the repentance is to mortify himself with great mortification and humbling, in place of the heating up he did to himself, and through this he merits the attribute of humility, which is above the place of repentance — and there is nothing that is not corrected by its opposite. And likewise, when he merits Chochmah, and draws from Chochmah the light of Torah to Yesod, to bestow it upon Malchut, corresponding to the drops of seed drawn from the brain to the covenant. And likewise, by drawing the supernal secrets from the secret of Da'at to Yesod, he also corrects the blemish, for through this the Shechinah is illuminated through Yesod, as explained in Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar, 94a). In short, there is nothing that is not corrected by repentance, and what is explained in the Zohar, that it does not depend on repentance, means that his repentance is difficult — and this too is part of the difficulty of repentance, that they show him that it does not depend on [ordinary] repentance; but there is nothing that stands before repentance. And even if you have heard "return, you backsliding children," except for so-and-so, as in the case of Elisha Acher ["the other one"], do not worry, for Elisha Acher was ultimately accepted even though he did not repent (Chagigah 15b) — all the more so, if he had repented, it would have benefited him even more; it was only that the gates of repentance were closed before him, and he needed to plead until the gate opened. This is what our Sages of blessed memory said (Pesachim 86b): whatever the master of the house tells you to do, do — except "go out." "The master of the house" is the Holy One, blessed be He: whatever He tells you to do among the commandments, do; except "go out" — if He tells you "go out of My house and do not enter," as in the case of Elisha Acher, do not listen to Him, but enter into repentance, for this is truly the master of the house's desire — He is only testing you.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:27: One must persist in repentance year after year, and not forget how many times he angered his Creator, for all his sins are counted and written down; and if not, Lilith is ready to exact from him the sum of his sins, for each time he warmed himself between her thighs, there he shall fall and not rise, until all the evil is consumed — for the Holy One, blessed be He, gives the wicked the strength to bear their punishment, and for each and every heating he is punished anew. The reason is as it is said (Genesis 39:10), "to lie beside her, to be with her" — and they said (Yoma 35b), "to lie beside her" in this world, "to be with her" in the World to Come, until he receives his punishment, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, said (Zohar, portion Pekudei, in the chambers of impurity, Chamber 2, 263b) that there is his punishment — we shall not copy his words there; see there. Therefore his repentance is difficult, since he must do repentance for each and every time he heated himself by emitting seed in vain.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:28: Further, my teacher, peace be upon him, wrote regarding "and Er, Judah's firstborn, and Onan" of whom it is said that "the LORD put them to death," and our Sages of blessed memory explained (tractate Kallah, ch. 3) that from here we learn that one who emits seed in vain is liable to death at the hands of Heaven. The reason is as explained above: since that drop emitted in vain did not enter a female, the external force is immediately present there and takes that evil heat, and seizes the soul that would have been fit to come through that drop; thus the external force holds all those souls fit to have come through those drops. And when a person marries a woman and has not done the proper repentance, the external force brings there those pure souls seized in her hand, and his children die while young, in the grip of their [demonic] mother, as explained in the Sava (portion Mishpatim, 96b). And in his suffering over the death of his children, what he was liable for — death at the hands of Heaven — is atoned for him, since he too has in some sense died, provided he repents from then on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:29: Regarding this sin it is said (Jeremiah 2:34), "also on your skirts is found the blood of the souls of the innocent poor." And likewise what our Sages of blessed memory explained (Niddah 13a), which we copied at the beginning of the chapter, "slaughterers of the children" (Isaiah 57:5) — that this one actually slaughters his own children, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in portion Vayechi (219b), which we copied above. Therefore he does not see the face of the Shechinah, for the Shechinah is not revealed to him as it is revealed to other righteous men, unless he does the proper repentance, as will be explained. Thus far the summary of his intent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:30: Further, regarding one who emits seed in vain, the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Zohar, portion Emor, 90a), these are his words: come and see, whoever emits seed in vain does not merit to see the face of the Shechinah and is called "evil," as it is said (Psalms 5:5), "for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You" — this refers to one who emits it by his hand or by some other means. And should you say this applies also to one who emits it into a woman who does not conceive — likewise so, not [this is not different], as we have said. Therefore a person should ask of the Holy One, blessed be He, that He arrange for him a fit vessel, so that he not blemish his seed — for whoever emits his seed into an unfit vessel blemishes his seed. Woe to one who blemishes his seed. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:31: Regarding the merit of one who is careful about emitting seed in vain, it is explained in Tana d'Bei Eliyahu, brought in the Yalkut, portion Mishpatim (§361, 98c), on the verse "and he sent the young men of the children of Israel, and they offered burnt offerings" — these are his words: it is taught in the school of Eliyahu: this is what the verse says (Deuteronomy 33:26), "there is none like the God of Yeshurun" — fortunate is a person who has true words of Torah within him, from whom no seed has gone out in vain; even if he is an [ordinary] Israelite, he is worthy to offer a burnt-offering upon the altar like a High Priest, as it is said (Exodus 24:5), "and he sent the young men of the children of Israel." And whoever becomes lazy [i.e., restrains himself] from a transgression and does not do it, is nourished from the radiance of the Shechinah, as it is said (ibid. 24:11), "and they beheld God, and they ate and drank." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:32: Just as one must guard the covenant from emitting seed in vain, so one must guard it from a niddah, a maidservant, a foreign woman, and a harlot. This matter is explained in the Zohar (portion Beshalach, 60b), these are his words: Rabbi Yitzchak said, certainly whoever merits Tzadik merits Netzach and Hod, and these are the three with which the Community of Israel is blessed; and whoever merits them merits the Holy King, and enters into all four. Corresponding to these four, this holy sign [the covenant] is guarded from these four: guarding of the Community of Israel is guarding from a niddah; guarding of Tzadik is guarding from a maidservant; guarding of Netzach is guarding from a foreign woman; guarding of Hod is guarding from a harlot.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:33: Regarding this, "to the voice of the LORD your God" — this is the Community of Israel [which is] "your God" — through what do Israel merit to receive the face of the Shechinah? Through guarding from a niddah, and therefore we have learned, it is written (Leviticus 18:19), "and you shall not approach a woman in her menstrual impurity to uncover her nakedness" — what is "to uncover her nakedness"? This is the Community of Israel, and to this are bound and connected the other matters to which the Community of Israel is bound — and this has already been established.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:34: "And do what is right in His eyes" — this is Tzadik, as it is written (Psalms 34:16), "the eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous" — to guard from a maidservant. And this we have already established, as in (Proverbs 30:23), "and a maidservant when she inherits from her mistress" — which causes the Tzadik to attach himself to the maidservant.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:35: "And give ear to His commandments" — this is Netzach, to guard against dealing falsely with it, that this sign not enter a foreign woman's daughter — not to deal falsely with Netzach, as it is written (1 Samuel 15:29), "and also the Netzach [Eternity/Glory] of Israel will not lie [yeshaker]." And whoever guards this fulfills His commandments, as it is written (Exodus 34:14), "for you shall not bow down to another god."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:36: "And keep all His statutes" — this is Hod, to guard against a harlot. This is explained as we have learned: Rabbi Yehuda said, what is the meaning of what is written (Psalms 45:4), "gird your sword upon your thigh, mighty one, your glory [hodcha] and your majesty"? Rather, whoever equips himself and places the fear of a sharp, powerful sword against it, upon the thigh — what is "upon the thigh"? This is the holy sign, as in (Genesis 24:2), "place, please, your hand under my thigh."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:37: Another interpretation: "gird your sword" — meaning, be diligent and overpower your evil inclination, which is your sword, "upon the thigh" — upon that holy sign, to guard it; and if he guards it, then he is called "mighty," and the Holy One, blessed be He, clothes him in His garments — and what are the garments of the Holy One, blessed be He? Hod and Netzach, as it is written (Psalms 104:1), "You are clothed in glory [hod] and majesty [hadar]" — here too, "your glory [hodcha] and your majesty [hadarcha]." And then a person attaches himself to the Holy King properly; from then on, "all the disease that I placed upon Egypt I will not place upon you, for I am the LORD your healer." Thus far his words. From this statement we learn the matter of guarding the covenant regarding these four mentioned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:38: Now, as part of guarding [oneself from] a niddah, one must be careful not to touch her, as the halakhic authorities have elaborated at length; therefore one must instruct the woman in the laws of niddah — the wearing of a white garment and its changing, the laws of interposition [chatzitzah] and immersion — for there are several matters in which the woman may not know, and one might come to have relations with a niddah [unknowingly]. And it is possible that Rashbi, peace be upon him, intended this in his statement regarding niddah, "and to this are bound and connected the other matters to which the Community of Israel is bound."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:39: Also explained in the statement is the merit of one who guards the covenant, called "mighty," and his merit in the World to Come — that the Holy One, blessed be He, clothes him in His garments, which are Netzach and Hod. And likewise his merit, as said at the end of the statement, "and then a person attaches himself to the Holy King" — this is Tiferet — and the end of the verse is fulfilled in him, "all the disease that I placed upon Egypt [I will not place upon you], for I am the LORD your healer" — for since he attaches himself to the Holy King, he draws healing from Arich Anpin; and by inference from the positive, you understand the negative [i.e., disease] does not apply, God forbid.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:40: Likewise in Midrash Yalkut they expounded the verse (Song of Songs 3:7), "each man with his sword upon his thigh," as referring to the warning regarding the covenant. These are his words: another interpretation, "each man with his sword upon his thigh" — this is circumcision; "from the fear of the nights" — for they are careful about the sin that resembles the night. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:41: Regarding the blemish of the covenant with another man's wife, or one who has relations with a niddah, a maidservant, a foreign woman, or a harlot — these are explained in the Zohar and in the midrashim of our Sages, and we have seen fit to copy some of their words so that the sinner, hearing the punishment, will fear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:42: They said in Midrash Rabbah, portion Ki Tisa (Bamidbar Rabbah 9:7), on the verse (Micah 2:10), "arise and go, for this is not the resting place, because of impurity that destroys, and a grievous destruction": the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, for other transgressions I would be patient with you, but since you have spread out in adultery — "arise and go." What is "a grievous destruction [chevel nimratz]"? I said (Deuteronomy 32:9), "for the LORD's portion is His people, Jacob is the cord [chevel] of His inheritance" — I took Jacob and he was My portion, since his seed was like a cord that is intertwined, one with another, for they were all properly attributed, children of their [true] fathers, and no other seed intervened between them, since they all guarded themselves from adultery and there was no illegitimacy there. How so? It is written (1 Chronicles 1:5) [error for the correct sequence, but as cited], "Elazar begot Pinchas, and Pinchas begot Avishua," and so all of them — the chain came thus. But you have entered upon your fellow's wife and defiled the inheritance — how can one count, "this is my son," when he is not his son, being illegitimate? You have severed the cord — hence "a grievous destruction." What is "nimratz"? [An acronym for] adulterer [no'ef], illegitimate [mamzer], wicked [rasha], oppressor [tzorer]. From this you learn that the decree of the Ten Tribes was sealed only for the sin of adultery.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:43: And from where do we know that the decree of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin was sealed only for adultery? For Jeremiah cried out before God: in the days of Menasheh the children were children of their [true] fathers; now they are children of lewdness — this is what is written (Jeremiah 4:22), "for My people are foolish" etc. What is written at the end of the passage? (ibid. 5:8), "they were like well-fed horses roaming about, each neighing after his neighbor's wife." Even though they transgressed all the commandments and denied the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written (ibid. 5:12), "they have denied the LORD," He was patient with them; but for adultery the decree was sealed against them, for it is written after this (ibid. 5:9), "shall I not punish them for these things, says the LORD." The Holy One, blessed be He, said: for everything else I suppress My anger, but for lewdness I am angered; behold, I hand them over to kingdoms — this is what is written (ibid. 5:10), "go up upon her walls and destroy." Thus far his words. Further below in the same passage (Bamidbar Rabbah 9:12): they transgress the Ten Commandments — and so it says (Ecclesiastes 7:26), "and I find more bitter than death, the woman" — woe to the transgression through which one transgresses all Ten Commandments. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:44: And in Bereshit Rabbah (26:5), these are his words: Rabbi Simlai said, wherever you find lewdness, indiscriminate slaughter [andralmusia] comes to the world and kills good and bad alike. Rabbi Azariah and Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Simon, in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, said: for everything the Holy One, blessed be He, is patient, except for lewdness, as it is said (Genesis 6:2), "and the sons of God saw" etc. — what is written after it? (ibid. 6:6), "and the LORD said, I will blot out man." Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of Rabbi Pedayah: all that night Lot was seeking mercy for the people of Sodom, and they were accepting it from him; once they said to him (Genesis 19:5), "bring them out to us, that we may know them" — for intercourse — they said to him (ibid. 19:12), "do you have anyone else here?" [meaning:] "son-in-law," [as if to say] plead their case no more — from then on you have no argument in their defense. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:45: And in Bava Metzia (58b) we say: three go down to Gehinnom and do not come up, and these are they: one who gives his fellow a bad nickname, one who whitens his fellow's face [shames him] in public, and one who has relations with another man's wife. Thus far his words.
